$comment: THE REGISTER OF RULE I5, retired duplicates (ADR 0014; governance.md section 3.1). Every member a cut-over removed
from this repository because a shared library now implements it, by its fully qualified name, with the milestone
that removed it and what replaced it. Rule I5 refuses a declaration of any of these names anywhere in the JavaScript
family's product sources, so a duplicate the programme retired cannot come back unnoticed. An entry is never
removed; a decision that reinstates a member removes its entry in the same change and says why.
SJL-3.4 (JSD-0065): the number-conversion area. What stays of JsNumberFormat (the shared strings of the commonest
Numbers, ToUintString and TrimWhiteSpace) and JsObject.IsArrayIndex and JsRealm.ObjectIsCanonicalNumeric, which
became adapters, are not here: they exist, and hold no algorithm.
SJL-4.4 (JSD-0069): the numerics area. A type declared directly in a namespace is registered by its own name. What
stays as adapters is not here: JsBigInt, the value wrapper whose operations are one line over BigIntMath and
BigIntText; JsElements.Narrow; JsRealm.MathHypotOperands and MathSumPrecise, which keep the coercion, the iteration and
the charges; JsRealm.BinaryToIndex, which keeps the coercion and the RangeError; and JavaScriptValue.ToInt32 and
ToUint32, public forwarders.
SJL-5.4 (JSD-0071): the text area. What stays as adapters is not here: StringPadTo, which converts the filler and maps
the status to RangeError; JsRealm.StringSubstitute and RegExpSubstitute, which evaluate the shared parser's parts;
RegExpAdvanceIndex and ArrayRelative, one line each; GlobalUriAnswer, which maps a status to URIError; the Base64
option readers, receiver, destination and result; JsonRead and JsonBuild with its object and array halves, which
build the values, the records and the errors; JsonApplySpace; and JsJsonModule.TryTranslate, the writer.
SJL-6.4 (JSD-0073): the Date area. What stays as adapters is not here: JsRealm.DateParseText, which charges the one
unit beyond the shared parser's and reads a local result in this profile's zone; DateTimeText, toTimeString's
TimeString and TimeZoneString; DateFromFields, DateSetTimeFields and DateSetDateFields, which keep the conversion and
its order; JsTemporalCore.AddDays, one line; JsLocalTime.From, which reads the shared field operations; and
JsZone.MondayFirst, which maps the shared WeekDay to the zone rules' Monday 0.
SJL-7.4 (JSD-0075, applying JSD-0074): the Unicode area, whose owner is Broiler.Unicode. Format's lookups, its
lexical classes and its folding and string-property readers are registered by type; so are the profile's
segmentation types. What stays as adapters is not here: the matcher's JsRegExpCase and its class sets, which call
the owner; JsRealm.FunctionIsNativeName and RegExpEscapeCodePoint, which ask the owner's lexical classes; and
JsRealm.Segmenter's objects and iterators, which ask the Intl data's segmentation through Format's
IJsTextSegmentation; and, beside normalization and casing, JsRealm.NormalizeText, StringChangeCase and TransformCase,
which keep the form's and the locale's resolution, the language pass's charge and the RangeError, and call the owner.
SJL-8.5 (JSD-0077, applying JSD-0076): the time-zone and calendar area, whose shared home is
Broiler.ECMAScript.Algorithms' Time namespace. The zone decoder's types and the calendar table's reader are
registered by type. What stays as adapters is not here: JsTemporal's zone operations (ParseZone, RulesOf,
OffsetNanosecondsFor, PossibleEpochNs, Disambiguate, EpochNsFor, StartOfDay, NextTransition, PreviousTransition and
TimeZoneEquals), which convert the profile's values, call ZonedTime and map its status to a RangeError in ZoneError;
JsRealm.ResolveTimeZone, which keeps the option's conversion and its two RangeErrors and asks OffsetTimeZones and the
database; JsZoneNames, which reads the database's regions, rules and daylight flag; the calendar systems' Year, which
reads CalendarYears through JsCalendarSystem.SharedYear; and JsIntlTables.TimeZones and Calendars, which build the
database and the tables once per data instance. JsZone.MondayFirst, which SJL-6.4's paragraph names as an adapter
that stays, went with its type: the zone rules it fed are the shared library's.
SJL-10.4 (JSD-0079, applying JSD-0078): the Temporal core, whose shared home is Broiler.ECMAScript.Algorithms'
Temporal namespace. The types deleted whole are registered by type: JsTemporalCore and the records it declared
(JsIsoDate, JsTimeRecord, JsIsoDateTime, JsDateDuration, JsInternalDuration and TemporalUnit), the parser's
TemporalGoal and JsTemporalParse, JsCalendarDate, JsDifferenceSettings, JsPrecision, JsFraction, JsRelativeTo and
JsNudge, and JsCalendars.cs's types. The members cut from the types that stay are registered by member: JsTemporal's
option rules, calendars, strings and duration arithmetic, JsTemporalParser's productions and parse state, and
JsCalendarFields' Has and CopyFrom. What stays as adapters is not here: JsTemporalParser's Parse, Instant,
Duration, CalendarString and TimeZoneString, which call TemporalGrammar and raise each TemporalParseError as a
RangeError; JsTemporal's option reads (Overflow, Show*Option, RoundingModeOption, RoundingIncrement,
FractionalSecondDigits, UnitOption, DifferenceSettingsOf), which read in the specification's order and hold each
value to TemporalOptionRules; the calendar adapters (CanonicalizeCalendar, CalendarIdOf, Calendars, PrepareFields,
MergeFields, DateFromFields, YearMonthFromFields, MonthDayFromFields, DateAdd, IsoToDate and DateToFields), which call
TemporalCalendars and map each CalendarStatus in CalendarError; RelativeToOption and InterpretDateTimeOffset, which
resolve relativeTo and a wall time's instant; TimeZoneOf, which hands a zone to the core as TemporalTimeZone; and
the realm files' methods, which keep their reads and map each TemporalStatus in StatusError. JsTemporalCore.AddDays,
which SJL-6.4's paragraph names as an adapter that stays, went with its type, and so did the calendar systems' Year
and JsCalendarSystem.SharedYear, which SJL-8.5's paragraph names: the shared calendars read CalendarYears themselves.
